summary: New announcements: Key Updates on Immigration Policies (September 04, 2026)

lastAnalysis.summary: Recent USCIS announcements highlight significant changes in immigration regulations, including new rules for children of foreign government employees, updates on the Diversity Visa program, and the introduction of new forms. These updates reflect ongoing legal challenges and efforts to streamline processes for applicants.

alerts.summary: The Department of Homeland Security has issued an interim final rule allowing certain children born in the U.S. to foreign government employees to register as lawful permanent residents. This change aims to provide a pathway for these children, who may have been previously ineligible due to their parents' non-citizen status, thereby enhancing their stability and integration into U.S. society.
alerts.title: DHS Announces Rule for Certain Children Born in the United States to Foreign Government Employees

alerts.summary: A U.S. District Court has temporarily vacated a policy affecting the adjudication of Diversity Visa applications, requiring USCIS to resume processing these applications without applying the previous hold policy. This ruling is significant for applicants who have been waiting for their status adjustments, as it may expedite their cases and provide relief from previous restrictions.
alerts.title: Court Order on Diversity Immigrant Visa Program Hold Policy

alerts.summary: USCIS is opening a new international field office in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, to enhance its operations in the region, particularly in fraud prevention. This office will facilitate better service delivery for applicants in Ethiopia and surrounding areas, improving the efficiency of immigration processes and addressing concerns about fraudulent applications.
alerts.title: USCIS Opens New International Field Office in Ethiopia to Support Fraud Prevention

alerts.summary: A court has issued an order enjoining certain hold policies that affected immigration applications. This decision is crucial as it may lead to the resumption of processing for many applicants who were impacted by these policies, thereby restoring their opportunities for adjustment of status and other immigration benefits.
alerts.title: Recent Court Order on Hold Policies

alerts.summary: USCIS will release a revised edition of Form I-485 on September 18, 2026, with older versions being rejected thereafter. This update is essential for applicants seeking to adjust their status, as using outdated forms could lead to delays or denials of their applications, emphasizing the need for practitioners to stay informed about form changes.
alerts.title: USCIS to Publish New Edition of Form I-485; Older Editions Will Be Rejected Starting Sept. 18

alerts.summary: USCIS has updated its guidance on how to assess whether an applicant for adjustment of status is likely to become a public charge. This clarification is significant as it provides clearer criteria for applicants, potentially affecting their eligibility and the documentation required to support their applications.
alerts.title: USCIS Issues Guidance on Making Public Charge Inadmissibility Determination

alerts.summary: Revised editions of Form I-539 and Form I-765 will be published on September 15, 2026, with older versions being rejected thereafter. This change is crucial for applicants seeking to extend or change their nonimmigrant status or apply for employment authorization, as using outdated forms could hinder their applications.
alerts.title: USCIS to Publish New Editions of Form I-539 and Form I-765; Older Editions Will Be Rejected Starting Sept. 15

alerts.summary: DHS has introduced an interim final rule mandating electronic filing for certain immigration forms. This move aims to enhance national security and streamline processing, which will require applicants and practitioners to adapt to new filing procedures, potentially improving efficiency but also necessitating adjustments in how applications are submitted.
alerts.title: USCIS To Require Electronic Filing of Forms: Strengthening National Security

alerts.summary: USCIS is clarifying that applicants must establish eligibility for immigration benefits at the time of filing. This change aims to reduce frivolous requests and improve the integrity of the immigration process, which may lead to stricter scrutiny of applications and a need for applicants to provide more comprehensive evidence upfront.
alerts.title: USCIS to Reduce Frivolous Immigration Benefits Requests by Reinforcing Evidence Standards

alerts.summary: USCIS has announced that it has reached the cap for H-1B visa petitions for fiscal year 2027. This announcement is critical for employers and foreign workers, as it indicates that no further petitions will be accepted for this fiscal year, impacting hiring plans and immigration strategies for many organizations.
alerts.title: USCIS Reaches Fiscal Year 2027 H-1B Cap

summary: New news releases: Crackdown on Immigration Fraud (September 03, 2026)

lastAnalysis.summary: Recent USCIS news releases highlight a significant crackdown on immigration fraud, including indictments related to false claims for citizenship and marriage fraud schemes. These actions signal a robust enforcement approach by USCIS and the Department of Justice, emphasizing the importance of integrity in the immigration process and the consequences of fraudulent activities.

alerts.summary: A naturalized U.S. citizen has been indicted for allegedly lying about his criminal history to gain citizenship. This case underscores the ongoing efforts by federal authorities to ensure that individuals who commit serious crimes do not benefit from the immigration system, reinforcing the integrity of U.S. citizenship.
alerts.title: Naturalized U.S. Citizen Indicted for Lying to Obtain U.S. Citizenship After Committing Felonies

alerts.summary: Federal prosecutors have indicted a Peruvian national for marriage-related immigration fraud, with USCIS playing a key role in the investigation. This case highlights the agency's commitment to combating fraudulent immigration practices and ensuring that marriage-based immigration benefits are not misused.
alerts.title: Illegal Alien Indicted in Marriage-Related Immigration Fraud

alerts.summary: An aunt and her nephew, a U.S. Airman, have been arrested for allegedly lying about their relationship to secure immigration benefits. This case illustrates the lengths to which individuals may go to exploit the immigration system and the vigilance of authorities in addressing such schemes.
alerts.title: Aunt and U.S. Airman Nephew Arrested in Immigration Fraud Scheme

alerts.summary: The Department of Homeland Security has proposed a new fee of $103,265 for H-1B cap-subject petitions, including those eligible for the advanced degree exemption. This proposal signals a potential shift in the financial landscape for employers seeking to hire foreign workers, reflecting ongoing discussions about the H-1B program's impact on the U.S. labor market.
alerts.title: DHS Proposes Additional H-1B Fee

alerts.summary: A Chinese national has been charged with voter fraud for submitting a fraudulent voter registration and ballot during the 2024 presidential election. This case raises concerns about the integrity of the electoral process and the importance of ensuring that only eligible individuals participate in elections.
alerts.title: Chinese Alien Charged with Voter Fraud in Massachusetts

alerts.summary: A Cuban national has pleaded guilty to charges related to alien smuggling and asylum fraud, with USCIS's involvement in the investigation. This case highlights the agency's role in tackling complex immigration-related crimes and the importance of maintaining the integrity of the asylum process.
alerts.title: Cuban Alien Pleads Guilty to Role in International Alien Smuggling, Asylum Fraud, and Money Laundering

alerts.summary: USCIS has been instrumental in the indictment of 11 individuals involved in orchestrating over 1,000 sham marriages for immigration benefits. This significant action demonstrates the agency's commitment to combating large-scale immigration fraud and protecting the integrity of the marriage-based immigration system.
alerts.title: USCIS Plays Key Role in Takedown of Decade-Long Marriage Fraud Ring

alerts.summary: A case has been filed to denaturalize an individual who allegedly obtained U.S. citizenship using a false identity. This action reflects the ongoing efforts by USCIS and the Department of Justice to ensure that citizenship is granted only to those who meet the legal requirements and do not engage in fraudulent activities.
alerts.title: Denaturalization Case Filed Against Man Who Procured U.S. Citizenship Under False Identity

alerts.summary: A Miami resident has been charged with defrauding the U.S. immigration system in connection with a national health care fraud investigation. This case highlights the intersection of immigration and health care fraud, emphasizing the need for vigilance in both areas.
alerts.title: Miami Man Charged With Defrauding U.S. Immigration System as Part of a National Health Care Takedown

alerts.summary: The Justice Department has filed a record number of denaturalization cases against 25 individuals accused of serious crimes. This unprecedented action signals a strong stance against criminal behavior among naturalized citizens and reinforces the importance of maintaining the integrity of the naturalization process.
alerts.title: Justice Department Files Record 25 Denaturalization Cases Against Naturalized Criminals Including Attempted Murderers, Spousal Abusers, and Child Sex Offenders

summary: New policy guidance: Key Policy Updates Overview (September 09, 2026)

lastAnalysis.summary: Recent updates to the USCIS Policy Manual reflect significant changes in immigration procedures, particularly regarding the registration of children born to foreign government employees, naturalization processes, and public charge inadmissibility. These changes aim to clarify eligibility criteria, enhance procedural integrity, and ensure compliance with legal standards, impacting applicants, practitioners, and USCIS officers alike.
lastAnalysis.title: Key Policy Updates Overview

updates.summary: This update introduces new policy guidance for registering children born to foreign government employees as lawful permanent residents. The inclusion of definitions for key terms clarifies the eligibility criteria, which will streamline the application process for affected families and provide clearer instructions for USCIS officers.

chapters.title: 7 USCIS-PM O.3 - Chapter 3 - Children Born in the United States to Foreign Government Employees
12 USCIS-PM A.2 - Chapter 2 - Born in the United States and Becoming a U.S. Naturalized Citizen

updates.title: Registration of Lawful Permanent Residence for Children Born to Foreign Government Employees in the United States

updates.summary: This update rescinds a previous policy that restricted nonprofit organizations from participating in naturalization ceremonies. By allowing these organizations to assist with voter registration, new citizens will have immediate access to voting resources, enhancing civic engagement and ensuring that eligible voters can register promptly.

chapters.title: 12 USC-PM J.5 - Chapter 5 - Administrative Naturalization Ceremonies

updates.title: Non-Governmental, Nonpartisan Organization Voter Registration Services at Administrative Naturalization Ceremonies

updates.summary: This guidance reintroduces personal investigations for naturalization applicants, emphasizing the need for thorough verification of applicants' information. This change aims to enhance the integrity of the naturalization process, potentially leading to more rigorous scrutiny of applications and impacting applicants who may need to provide additional evidence.

chapters.title: 12 USCIS-PM B.1 - Chapter 1 - Purpose and Background
12 USCIS-PM B.2 - Chapter 2 - Background Investigation and Security Checks
12 USCIS-PM B.3 - Chapter 3 - Naturalization Examination

updates.title: Investigations and Examinations for Naturalization Eligibility

updates.summary: This update revises the public charge inadmissibility guidance following the rescission of the 2022 Final Rule. The new guidance clarifies the criteria for determining public charge status, which may affect applicants' eligibility for various immigration benefits, thereby influencing their application strategies.

chapters.title: 8 USCIS-PM G - Part G - Public Charge Ground of Inadmissibility

updates.title: Public Charge Ground of Inadmissibility

updates.summary: This temporary update reinstates previous guidance allowing nonprofit organizations to assist in voter registration during naturalization ceremonies, pending litigation outcomes. This change ensures that new citizens can register to vote immediately, enhancing their civic participation.

chapters.title: 12 USC-PM J.5 - Chapter 5 - Administrative Naturalization Ceremonies

updates.title: Participation of Non-Governmental Organizations at Administrative Naturalization Ceremonies

updates.summary: This update removes references to the Diplomatic List, which is no longer published. This change simplifies the policy manual and reflects current practices, ensuring that officers and applicants are aligned with the latest procedural standards.

chapters.title: 7 USCIS-PM O.3 - Chapter 3 - Children Born in the United States to Foreign Government Employees
12 USCIS-PM H.3 - Chapter 3 - U.S. Citizens at Birth (INA 301 and 309)

updates.title: Lists of Foreign Diplomatic Officers Accredited to the United States

updates.summary: This guidance allows USCIS officers to recommend DNA testing as optional evidence to establish genetic relationships when primary evidence is lacking. This change provides applicants with an additional avenue to substantiate their claims, potentially easing the burden of proof in certain cases.

chapters.title: 1 USCIS-PM E.6 - Chapter 6 - Evidence
4 USCIS-PM C.4 - Chapter 4 - Documentation and Evidence
5 USCIS-PM C.7 - Chapter 7 - Documentation and Evidence
5 USCIS-PM D.3 - Chapter 3 - Identity and Age
12 USCIS-PM H.2 - Chapter 2 - Definition of Child and Residence for Citizenship and Naturalization

updates.title: Suggesting DNA Testing When Issuing a Request for Additional Evidence

updates.summary: This update revises the standards for evidence, RFEs, and NOIDs, aiming to clarify the expectations for applicants and the decision-making process for officers. This change may lead to more consistent application of evidentiary standards, impacting how applicants prepare their submissions.

chapters.title: 1 USCIS-PM E.6 - Chapter 6 - Evidence
1 USCIS-PM E.9 - Chapter 9 - Rendering a Decision
1 USCIS-PM E.10 - Chapter 10 - Post-Decision Actions

updates.title: Evidence, Requests for Evidence, and Notices of Intent to Deny

updates.summary: This update consolidates and updates guidance regarding the role of attorneys and representatives in immigration proceedings. By clarifying the responsibilities and conduct expected from legal representatives, this change aims to enhance the integrity of the representation process for applicants.

chapters.title: 1 USCIS-PM D.1 - Chapter 1 - Purpose and Background
1 USCIS-PM D.2 - Chapter 2 - Representation
1 USCIS-PM D.3 - Chapter 3 - Other Representatives
1 USCIS-PM D.4 - Chapter 4 - Establishing and Changing Representation
1 USCIS-PM D.5 - Chapter 5 - Professional Conduct and Reporting Misconduct

updates.title: Attorneys and Representatives

updates.summary: This update clarifies the signature requirements for submitting immigration benefit requests, ensuring that applicants and their representatives understand the necessary documentation. This change aims to reduce errors in submissions and improve processing efficiency.

chapters.title: 1 USCIS-PM B.2 - Chapter 2 - Signatures
7 USCIS-PM A.3 - Chapter 3 - Filing Instructions

updates.title: Signature Requirements for the Submission of Benefit Requests

updates.summary: This update implements regulatory changes regarding the duration a nonimmigrant religious worker must remain outside the U.S. after reaching the maximum stay. This change aims to provide greater flexibility for religious organizations and their employees, potentially facilitating smoother transitions for those in religious roles.

chapters.title: 2 USCIS-PM O.7 - Chapter 7 - Period of Stay

updates.title: Improving Continuity for Religious Organizations and Their Employees

updates.summary: This update reaffirms the use of deferred action as a discretionary tool for USCIS. This clarification may impact applicants seeking relief from removal or other forms of immigration enforcement, as it emphasizes the agency's ability to exercise discretion in individual cases.

chapters.title: 1 USCIS-PM I - Part I – Deferred Action

updates.title: Deferred Action as an Extraordinary Use of Prosecutorial Discretion

updates.summary: This technical update revises footnotes in the Policy Manual to reflect the latest version of the U.S. Department of State’s Exchange Visitors Skills List. While primarily technical, it ensures that the policy manual remains current and accurate, which is essential for practitioners and applicants referencing this list.

chapters.title: 2 USCIS-PM D.1 - Chapter 1 - Purpose and Background
2 USCIS-PM D.3 - Chapter 3 - Terms and Conditions of J Exchange Visitor Status

updates.title: Technical Update - 2024 U.S. Department of State Exchange Visitors Skills List

updates.summary: This update clarifies the policies and requirements for aliens seeking classification as VAWA self-petitioners. By providing clearer guidelines, this change aims to facilitate the application process for survivors of domestic violence, ensuring they understand their rights and the necessary steps to seek relief.

3 USCIS-PM D.4 - Chapter 4 - Filing Requirements
3 USCIS-PM D.5 - Chapter 5 - Adjudication
3 USCIS-PM D.6 - Chapter 6 - Post-Adjudicative Matters

updates.title: Violence Against Women Act

updates.summary: This update clarifies the applicability of provisions under 8 U.S.C. 1367, which protect certain information for individuals seeking immigration relief. By resolving technical errors in safe address procedures, this change enhances the confidentiality protections for vulnerable populations, ensuring their safety during the immigration process.

chapters.title: 1 USCIS-PM A.7 - Chapter 7 - Privacy and Confidentiality

updates.title: Applicability of 8 U.S.C. 1367(a)(1) and (a)(2) Provisions

lastAnalysis.title: Fluctuating I-130 Processing Times
lastAnalysis.analysis: The processing times for Form I-130 show considerable variation across different service centers and categories. Immediate Relatives (IR) generally experience shorter processing times compared to Family Preference categories (F11, F21, F31, F41), which are subject to longer delays. Notably, some categories have processing times listed as 'See notes', indicating that USCIS is prioritizing these cases based on the Department of State Visa Bulletin constraints rather than adhering to fixed timelines. This suggests a strategic allocation of resources to align with visa availability, impacting the predictability of processing times.
